survivors.reason: A block that runs between a downgrade and its re-upgrade is below the nomenclature revision, so it must ask the database for the names that revision restored. The pre-cut spelling is the schema at that point, not residue.

survivors.verification: Two named files and three tokens; the downgrade/re-upgrade tests fail if the name is wrong in either direction, so an entry that stopped being needed cannot sit here unnoticed.

survivors.reason: These three files are the rename's specification and the tests that hold it, so every Task-domain token in them is either the left-hand side of a rule, a probe pattern the residue scanner matches with, or a fixture asserting that a rewrite happened. A manifest mapping task_memory to intent_memory has to contain the literal task_memory; the scanner has to contain the probes it scans with, which is why entries like TASK = "task" and ambiguous_task_ids appear; and the tests have to contain both spellings to assert anything at all. Renaming any of it would delete the rename.
survivors.immutability_basis: Left-hand side and probe vocabulary of the rename it defines; removing the pre-image removes the rule.
survivors.verification: The breadth is on the token side and the narrowness is on the path side, deliberately: three exact files, none of them a product module, so no shipped surface can hide behind this. Enumerating tokens instead was tried and is the wrong shape -- it silently stops covering the engine the moment a probe is added, which is exactly when the check would start reporting on its own scanner. What still constrains these files is stronger than a residue scan: the engine's unit suite asserts every rule's pre-image and post-image, and check reports a digest mismatch the moment the manifest's own bytes move.

survivors.reason: The same class as SV-05, which covers artifact_semantics_v1 only. These four V1 fixture subtrees carry the V1 field spelling because their digests identify these exact bytes; the V1 verification suite reads them to prove the product can still verify what it signed before the rename.
survivors.immutability_basis: Signed V1 canonical artifact, identified by digest.
survivors.verification: Regenerating the V1 vectors must leave every one of these subtrees byte-identical, which the frozen-tree digest asserts.

survivors.reason: Widens SV-07, which admitted only the scope enumeration. The generator emits the V1 field names into the V1 subtrees, so those literals are part of what it must keep producing byte-for-byte; renaming them would regenerate different bytes and invalidate every V1 digest.
survivors.immutability_basis: Generator of signed V1 canonical artifacts.
survivors.verification: Regenerate and diff: the V1 subtrees must be byte-identical afterwards.

survivors.reason: Active code that must keep naming the V1 field set, because the product authors V2 and still verifies V1. These are V1 schema literals and V1 artifact-kind values, not relational columns: authoring_profile_shapes.py binds them into the _V1 schema constants and says so at its own definitions, and canonical.py holds task_summary and intent_summary together in one optional-field set precisely because both versions are live. Renaming them does not rename a concept, it redefines what V1 means, and installing a renamed postimage was measured to turn twelve frozen fixture vectors red, four of them in a subtree this manifest marks immutable.
survivors.immutability_basis: Field names of a published V1 contract the product still verifies against.
survivors.verification: The V1 fixture vectors and the canonical-manifest suite are the control: they read these constants, so a rename here goes red there. Scoped to the two schema modules and the three suites that assert on them; no V2 authoring path is admitted, and the V2 spellings are unaffected.
